newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia skilled vacancies falls in July.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia skilled vacancies falls in July.

text.p: The Australian government's skilled vacancies index fell 0.7 percent in July from June and was unchanged from a year earlier, the Employment Department said on Thursday.
The department said the latest monthly fall continued the downward trend of recent months, which has seen the index fall steadily to 142 from 149 in February.

Increases were recorded in five of the 16 occupational groups, with the biggest rise a 6.3 percent jump for medical and science technical officers grouping. Building trades were up 5.3 percent in the month and computing professionals 3.2 percent.

The strongest falls among the 10 groups which declined were a 12.1 percent drop in the health diagnosis and treatment practitioners sector, 3.1 percent in building professionals and engineers and 2.7 percent in the other professionals grouping.
The monthly index is 115.2 percent above the recession low of 66 in mid-1991.
Only two states recorded an increase -- Queensland with 2.3 percent and Western Australia with 0.9 percent.
The Northern Territory and all other states fell -- except Victoria which remained unchanged -- with the biggest decline a 15.4 percent drop in Tasmania and a 4.2 percent fall in New South Wales.
However, the department cautions the results in Tasmania and the Territory are highly volatile because of the small sample.
The monthly index is based on a count of skilled vacancies advertisements in the major metropolitan newspaper for each state capital and the Northern Territory.
